questions.stem: A traveller wants to visit a malaria-endemic area and decides to take doxycycline as chemoprophylaxis. Which of the following is the correct method of chemoprophylaxis ?

options.label: A
options.text: The drug should be started 7 days before travel and continued for 2 weeks after leaving the malarious area

options.label: B
options.text: The drug should be started 2 days before travel and continued for 4 weeks after leaving the malarious area

options.label: C
options.text: The drug should be started 10 days before travel and continued for 3 weeks after leaving the malarious area

options.label: D
options.text: The drug should be started 15 days before travel and continued for 2 weeks after leaving the malarious area

questions.answerText: The drug should be started 2 days before travel and continued for 4 weeks after leaving the malarious area
questions.solutionHtml:
The drug should be started 2 days before travel and continued for 4 weeks after leaving the malarious area
  • Malaria chemoprophylaxis is recommended for travellers, migrant labourers and military personnel
  • Short-term chemoprophylaxis (less than 6 weeks)
  • Doxycycline: 100 mg daily in adults and 1.5 mg/kg body weight for children more than 8 years old.
  • The drug should be started 2 days before travel and continued for 4 weeks after leaving the malarious area.
  • Note: Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnant and lactating women and children less than 8 years.


Long-term chemoprophylaxis (more than 6 weeks)

  • Mefloquine:5 mg/kg body weight (up to 250 mg) weekly and should be administered two weeks before, during and four weeks after leaving the area.
  • Note: Mefloquine is contraindicated in cases with a history of convulsions, neuropsychiatric problems and cardiac conditions.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 875, 876

questions.stem: The rationale for combining metronidazole with a luminal amoebicidal agent in the treatment of amebiasis is :

options.label: A
options.text: Metronidazole is almost completely absorbed in the proximal intestine

options.label: B
options.text: Little therapeutic amount of Metronidazole reaches the colon

questions.solutionHtml:
Both are correct

The cornerstone of therapy for amebiasis is metronidazole or its analogue tinidazole

  • Metronidazole is so well absorbed in the gut, the very little therapeutic amount reaches the colon
  • It cannot act as luminal amoebicide
  • Therefore, patients with amebic colitis or amebic liver abscess should receive a luminal agent in addition to metronidazole to eradicate any E. histolytica trophozoites residing within the gut lumen


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 987

questions.stem: Among the following options, Anti-malarial used for resistant P. falciparum malaria in children is :
questions.solutionHtml:
Lumefantrine

Drugs used in the treatment of Chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria are:

  1. Artesunate
  2. Sulfadoxine
  3. Pyrimethamine
  4. Mefloquine
  5. Lumefantrine
  6. Quinine
  7. Doxycycline
